title: Integral closed subscheme tests and the generic witness on a proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\xi$ be its generic point, so $\overline{\{\xi\}}=C$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every integral closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], exactly one of the following holds: $i$ is an isomorphism over $C$; or there is a closed point $z\ne\xi$, meaning $\{z\}$ is closed, and an isomorphism $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ over $C$ identifying $i$ with the canonical residue-field morphism. Here $\operatorname{Spec}$ and $\kappa(z)=\mathcal O_{C,z}/\mathfrak m_z$ are as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-residue-field]. In the first case the coherent module $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_C$ [pqf-def-coherent] has support $C$, where $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=\{x:\mathcal G_x\ne0\}$ and stalks are [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Its generic stalk is $\kappa(\xi)$, annihilated by $\mathfrak m_\xi=0$, and has dimension one over $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Moreover $\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal O_C\cong\mathcal L$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and
$$\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_C)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=\deg_k(\mathcal L),$$
with Euler characteristic and degree as in [def-pc-euler-characteristic, def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, proof of condition (2): the dichotomy Z=X or a closed point and the witness O_X when Z=X (returned steps 4-5).

proof.text: Put $T=i(|Z|)$. By the definition of a closed immersion and integrality, $T$ is a nonempty irreducible closed subset of $C$. Scheme sobriety gives a unique $z\in T$ with $\overline{\{z\}}=T$. Suppose $T\ne C$. If $y\in T$ and $y\ne z$, then $\overline{\{y\}}\subseteq T$; equality would make $y$ a second generic point of $T$, so this inclusion is strict. The closure of a singleton is irreducible: any closed cover of it contains the point in one member, hence contains its entire closure in that member. Thus $\overline{\{y\}}\subsetneq T\subsetneq C$ is a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length two, contrary to $\dim C=1$. Therefore $T=\{z\}$ is closed. It cannot contain $\xi$, since a closed subset containing $\xi$ contains $C$. Finally $C$ is not a singleton: a singleton has no strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets and has dimension zero.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, condition (2); elementary expansion of its whole-curve/closed-point dichotomy, using Schemes Tag 01IS, lemma-scheme-sober

proof.text: Since $C$ and $Z$ are integral, both are reduced. If $T=C$, compare $i:Z\to C$ with the identity closed immersion of $C$. Uniqueness of the reduced induced closed subscheme on $T$ identifies them over $C$, so $i$ is an isomorphism. If $T=\{z\}$, the canonical morphism $j_z:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to C$ is a closed immersion by the closed-point residue-immersion criterion. Its source is integral, hence reduced: its only nonempty affine open is itself and its ring is the field $\kappa(z)$. Its image is $\{z\}$. Apply the same uniqueness theorem to $i$ and $j_z$ to obtain $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ over $C$. The alternatives are exclusive because their images are respectively $C$ and the proper singleton $\{z\}$.

source.place: Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, uniqueness; canonical residue-field map: Tag 01J9, lemma-characterize-points

proof.text: In the whole-curve case choose $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_C$. The proper-field invertible-coherence theorem, applied to $C$ and the given $\mathcal L$, gives coherence of $\mathcal O_C$ and $\mathcal L$. For every $x\in C$, the integral-scheme stalk theorem says $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ is an integral domain, hence is nonzero. The stalk of $\mathcal G$ is exactly $\mathcal O_{C,x}$, so the support specified in the statement is all of $C$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, condition (2), choice G=O_X; coherence: Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian

proof.text: At $\xi$, the same integral-scheme stalk theorem identifies $\mathcal G_\xi=\mathcal O_{C,\xi}$ as a field. The only proper ideal of a field is zero (a nonzero element generates $1$), so its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_\xi=0$. By the definition $\kappa(\xi)=\mathcal O_{C,\xi}/\mathfrak m_\xi$, the quotient map identifies $\mathcal G_\xi$ with $\kappa(\xi)$ as a module over the stalk ring. Its annihilation by $\mathfrak m_\xi$ follows from $\mathfrak m_\xi=0$. The singleton $\{1\}$ is a basis over this field: every element is its own scalar times $1$, and $a\cdot1=0$ forces $a=0$. The dimension is consequently one.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, final assertion; elementary residue-field and basis calculation

proof.text: For every open $U$, the balanced map $s\otimes a\mapsto as$ identifies $\mathcal L(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_C(U)}\mathcal O_C(U)$ with $\mathcal L(U)$, with inverse $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. The two composites are identities because $(as)\otimes1=s\otimes a$. These maps commute with restriction. Hence the presheaf tensor $P$ is isomorphic to the sheaf $\mathcal L$ by some $\alpha:P\to\mathcal L$. Its sheafification $P\to P^\#$ defines the sheaf tensor product. By the universal property, $\alpha$ factors uniquely as $\beta\circ(P\to P^\#)$ with $\beta:P^\#\to\mathcal L$, and $\alpha^{-1}$ followed by $P\to P^\#$ is a map $\gamma:\mathcal L\to P^\#$. Uniqueness of factorizations through $P\to P^\#$ gives $\gamma\beta=\mathrm{id}$, and $\beta\gamma=\mathrm{id}$ is immediate, so $P^\#\cong\mathcal L$. Thus $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_C\cong\mathcal L$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; explicit tensor-unit maps on sections

proof.text: The preceding isomorphism identifies $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_C$ with the coherent module $\mathcal L$. Cohomology, being a functor, sends this isomorphism to isomorphisms in every degree, so the alternating sums defining the two Euler characteristics agree. The definition of degree gives $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(C,\mathcal L)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$. Substituting yields $\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_C)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=\deg_k(\mathcal L)$, exactly the generic witness assertion in Tag 0AYV.
